html:
The Tamien are an Ohlone people of the Santa Clara Valley in California, around today's San Jose. Tamien was the name of a village and its people, who spoke Tamyen, one of the Ohlone languages.

They lived by gathering acorns and seeds, hunting and fishing along the creeks running into San Francisco Bay. In 1777 the Spanish founded Mission Santa Clara on their land, and many were brought into it, where disease killed large numbers. Today the Tamien Nation is an organisation of their descendants, not recognised by the federal government. To the east lived the Yokuts.
